headline: Make the coin a constant-revenue unit (about 0.055 US cents at a 50-coin US ad), price everything in ad-equivalents, burn coins only through a disclosed arena fee on staked duels plus drill/expedition entries, guarantee "one ad always buys one duel" in every geo, keep bots unstaked, and protect loss streaks only with levers that never touch questions, bots or opponents. The existing lib/economy/economy.mjs already has the right shape; its EU ad-reward numbers are wrong by about 2x against the only verifiable geo eCPM data, and India's eCPM is unverified anywhere reachable.

findings.finding: CURRENT STATE. /home/user/fact-duel/lib/economy/economy.mjs is already a pure, integer, identity-preserving reducer with: adReward by region (US 50, GB 45, DE 40, FR 40, IN 20, '*' 30), adDailyCap 20, adCooldownMs 45000, daily 30, practiceEntry 10, stakes [10,25,50,100,250], floor {coins 25, every 6h}, softCap 5000, a zero-sum stake()/receivePayout() pair, and an ltvCents() helper. It has, by construction, no notion of question difficulty or bot skill (the file's own header says so) and no rake. /home/user/fact-duel/lib/ledger/intents.mjs settles a real escrow account per room that must be exhausted exactly (a rake would need a burn leg). /home/user/fact-duel/lib/ads/provider.mjs keys payment on a per-completion adId and names four placements (coins, practice-entry, duel-entry, continue). The design below is a re-tune of these files, not a rewrite.
findings.evidence: Read lib/economy/economy.mjs (DEFAULT_CONFIG, earnFromAd, claimDaily, applyFloor, stake, receivePayout, enterPractice, affordability, ltvCents), lib/ledger/intents.mjs lines 55-102, lib/ads/provider.mjs.

findings.finding: THE UNIT. Define the coin as a constant-revenue unit anchored on the US: v = eCPM_US / (1000 x R_US). With R_US = 50 coins per ad and a US blended rewarded eCPM of $27.32 (mean of Tenjin/CAS.AI Q2 2024 iOS $24.39 and Android $30.25), v = $0.000546 per coin, i.e. about 0.055 US cents. Every other geo's ad reward is R_g = max(s_min, round5(R_US x eCPM_g / eCPM_US)). Applying that to the same source gives UK 35, DE 25, FR 20 coins per ad (revenue per coin 0.055 / 0.053 / 0.051 cents - flat within 7%). The current config's GB 45 / DE 40 / FR 40 over-pays the EU by roughly 1.3x / 1.6x / 2x against this data and should be replaced. Stake tiers stay GLOBAL in coins (10/25/50/100/250) so cross-geo duels are fair in revenue terms; what varies by geo is how many ads a tier costs.
findings.evidence: Tenjin/CAS.AI charts 'Average eCPM for Rewarded Ads by Country in Q2 2024' (iOS: US 24.39, KR 20.94, AU 19.91, JP 17.24, UK 16.76, CA 16.08, DE 12.20, RU 11.44, FR 10.87, BR 8.39; Android: US 30.25, CA 23.13, KR 22.01, UK 21.60, JP 14.70, DE 14.07, FR 9.58, RU 5.72, MX 3.44, BR 3.08) read from the chart images embedded at https://tenjin.com/blog/ad-mon-gaming-2026/ (files iOS_Rewarded-3.png and Android_Rewarded-4.png; the report says the eCPM portion is CAS.AI data, 6bn impressions, excluding kids apps). Arithmetic in scratchpad script.

findings.finding: INDIA IS NOT IN ANY VERIFIABLE eCPM TABLE REACHABLE. Tenjin's per-country rewarded charts stop at BR/MX/RU (lowest verified: Brazil Android $3.08, Mexico Android $3.44 in Q2 2024). Tenjin's own India article (5 Feb 2026) gives ARPPU ($3 in 2020 to $27 in 2025) and market CAGR (31%), but no eCPM. Business of Apps was reachable via curl but only carries global format averages (rewarded video $8.00 in 2019, $10.00 in 2023, $10.50 forecast 2024), not per-country. GameAnalytics and Appodeal benchmark tools are gated/empty (already recorded in public/product/investor/numbers.md). Therefore the India coin rate cannot be set from research; it must be set from the mediation dashboard's trailing-28-day eCPM after launch. The formula handles it: at any eCPM_IN below about $5.5 the floor rule R_g >= s_min = 10 binds, so India pays 10 coins per ad (the 'one ad buys one duel' guarantee) and revenue-per-coin in India is deliberately BELOW the anchor. That is a bounded, chosen subsidy, not an accident.
findings.evidence: https://tenjin.com/blog/the-mobile-gaming-market-in-india-aiming-for-the-middle/ (no eCPM); https://www.businessofapps.com/ads/research/mobile-app-advertising-cpm-rates/ (Artem Dogtiev, 27 Feb 2025; fetched via curl); Tenjin chart images listed above; public/product/investor/numbers.md section 5.1.

findings.finding: AD-RATE TRACKING RULE (so one ad is worth roughly the same revenue everywhere). Inputs: eCPM_g = trailing-28-day realised rewarded eCPM per country from the mediation layer, smoothed with an exponential moving average (alpha 0.3, weekly refresh) so the coin reward does not twitch with weekly auction noise. R_g = clamp(round5(R_US x eCPM_g / eCPM_US_ref), s_min, 3 x R_US). eCPM_US_ref is frozen per season (not live) so the US reward itself is stable; other geos float against it. Changes ship in the server config bundle the client already expects (economy.mjs comment: 'meant to be overridden by a bundle the server hands the client'). The reward shown on the button before the tap is the reward paid (AdMob: rewards are a whole-number 'reward amount' per ad unit; Google Play exempts only ads 'explicitly opted-in by users' from its Better Ads rules, so the offer must be explicit and pre-tap).
findings.evidence: https://support.google.com/admob/answer/7311747 (reward amount, frequency capping); https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9857753 ('This policy does not apply to rewarded ads which are explicitly opted-in by users'); lib/economy/economy.mjs header comment.

findings.finding: STAKE TIERS IN AD-EQUIVALENTS. Express the ladder as {0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5} ad-equivalents (AE) of the US reward = 10/25/50/100/250 coins, which is exactly the existing config, plus a 10-AE tier (500) unlocked only above the soft cap for hoarders. Session coin income for a US player who watches 2 ads per session: 2 x 50 + daily 30 spread over the median 3.85 sessions/day (about 8 per session) = about 108 coins per session, so the 1-AE tier (50) is 'half a session', the 2-AE tier is 'a full session', and 5 AE is 'two and a half sessions' - a ladder where the top tier is a meaningful but not ruinous swing. In DE (R=25) the same coin tiers cost twice the ads; in India at the floor (R=10) five times. The daily grant, streak and quest grants stay global in coins and are the equaliser for low-eCPM geos.
findings.evidence: GameAnalytics 2026 Mobile & PC Gaming Benchmarks, CY2025, 16,000+ games: median sessions/day 3.8-3.9, session length 3.1-3.5 min, daily playtime 12 min (https://www.gameanalytics.com/reports/2026-mobile-pc-gaming-benchmarks). Coin arithmetic from the geo table above.

findings.finding: GAMBLER'S RUIN SETS THE FLOOR SIZE. For a fair duel (p=0.5) with a 10% arena fee, the probability of hitting zero within n duels from a bankroll of k stake-units is: k=1: 75% in 2 duels, 88% in 10; k=2: 25% / 73%; k=3: 0% / 52%; k=5: 0% in 4 duels, 22% in 10, 44% in 20; k=10: 0.1% in 10, 6.5% in 20. So a player who enters a session with fewer than 3 units of their chosen tier will very likely bust inside that session. Design consequence: the client's stake picker should default to the tier where balance >= 5 x stake (Kelly for an even-money bet is f* = 2p - 1, which is 0 at p=0.5 - there is no positive-EV stake for a median player, so tier choice is a variance choice and the UI should say so), and the floor top-up should restore at least 2 x s_min. Recommended floor: top up TO 20 coins (2 min-stake duels or 2 drills), at most once per 6 h, never above the soft cap - a change from the current 25. Plus an always-available unstaked 'friendly' duel that pays XP/quest progress but no coins, so a player at zero is never locked out of playing even when the ad provider is unavailable (NullAdProvider case).
findings.evidence: Ruin probabilities computed by exact dynamic programming in the scratchpad script; closed forms for the fair and unfair cases per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambler%27s_ruin (P1 = n2/(n1+n2) fair; P1 = [1-(p/q)^n2]/[1-(p/q)^(n1+n2)] unfair); Kelly f* = p/l - q/g, even-money f* = 2p-1, 'betting an amount larger than the Kelly amount increases the risk of ruin' per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_criterion.

findings.finding: RAKE DECISION: TAKE A DISCLOSED 10% ARENA FEE ON THE POT AT TIERS >= 1 AE, 0% AT THE TWO MICRO TIERS. Math: with pot 2s and fee r, each player's expected burn per duel is r x s; break-even win rate becomes p* = 1/(2(1-r)) = 0.526 at 5% and 0.556 at 10%; a 50% player drifts -0.1 stake per duel at 10%. Why take it at all: in a P2P zero-sum economy the only sinks are entries and the fee, while ads and grants mint every session, so without a volume-scaled sink the population balance grows without bound. The fee is the auto-stabiliser: burn scales with play volume and with stake size, so it bites hardest exactly where hoarded coins are played. Steady-state balance: if players stake a fraction phi of bankroll per duel, play n_d duels per session and receive F coins of faucet per session, balance stabilises where n_d x r x phi x B = F, i.e. B* = F / (n_d x r x phi) = 100 / (2 x 0.10 x 0.10) = 5,000 coins - which is exactly the current soft cap, so the two mechanisms agree. At 5% the same arithmetic gives 10,000. Why not at micro tiers: the 10- and 25-coin tiers are the lockout-protection tiers and a fee there converts the floor grant into a treadmill. Honesty requirement: every 'winner takes the pot' string becomes 'winner takes the pot minus the 10-coin arena fee', shown before commit; the ledger gets a burn leg from escrow to a sink account so intents.mjs's 'escrow must settle to zero' invariant still holds.
findings.evidence: Formulas derived and computed in the scratchpad script; escrow invariant from lib/ledger/intents.mjs lines 75-102; disclosure duty from 15 U.S.C. 45(a)(1) ('unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce, are hereby declared unlawful', https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/45) and UCPD Arts 6-7 as applied by the CPC Network principles (price information is 'material information').

findings.finding: INFLATION ACCOUNTING (per player-session, US, base case). Faucets: 2 ads x 50 = 100; daily 30 / 3.85 sessions = 8; floor <= 20 per 6h (rare); quests/streaks - set the budget at <= 30 per day (8 per session). Total F about 116. Sinks: 2 duels at the 1-AE tier with 10% fee = 10; 1 practice entry = 10; expedition entry 50 once per 3 sessions = about 17. Total about 37. Net mint about +79 coins per player-session, so the median balance rises roughly 300 coins/day until stake tiers rise with it and the fee burn catches up (B* derivation above). That is acceptable ONLY because coins have no exit; the control levers, in order of use: (1) soft cap stops grants and the floor (already implemented); (2) fee escalates with tier (5% at 1 AE, 10% at 2-5 AE, 15% at 10 AE) so whales burn faster; (3) quest grants are paired with sinks (quest: 'play 3 staked duels' pays 30, but those duels burn about 15); (4) NEVER decay balances - a silent decay is the one sink that reads as theft and would itself be a hidden-cost practice. Monitor: total supply M(t), coins per DAU, and the sink/faucet ratio; target sinks/faucets >= 0.35 at launch rising to 0.6 by month 3 as tiers unlock.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic in the scratchpad script using the geo table and GameAnalytics medians; Machinations' F2P balancing method (sources/sinks, persona simulation, 'Premium as Shortcut', top-2% F2P outperforming 19% of buyers) at https://machinations.io/articles/balancing-f2p-economies-simulating-player-personas-and-progression-curves-with-machinations (Bogdan, Nov 2025); Adams & Dormans, Game Mechanics: Advanced Game Design (New Riders, 2012, ISBN 978-0-321-82027-3) for the source/drain/converter vocabulary (https://www.peachpit.com/store/game-mechanics-advanced-game-design-9780321820273); Lehdonvirta & Castronova, Virtual Economies: Design and Analysis (MIT Press, 2014, ISBN 0262535068).

findings.finding: HOARDING IS NOT AN ECONOMIC PROBLEM, ONLY AN ENGAGEMENT ONE. A whale who never watches ads costs nothing (no impression served) and supplies liquidity as an opponent; the only loss is the ads they would have watched. So do not punish hoarding; make spending attractive: the 5-AE and 10-AE tiers unlock at 1,000 and 5,000 coins, expeditions with 100-250-coin entries and cosmetic titles priced in coins (never money) give large balances somewhere to go, and the fee does the burning. Break-even skill with a 10% fee is 55.6%, so a genuinely strong player nets +0.08 stake per duel at p=0.6 and still accumulates; that is fine - they are the product's leaderboard content. The soft cap (grants stop at 5,000; ads always pay, because attention must always be honoured) is the only cap.
findings.evidence: Break-even and EV formulas computed in the scratchpad script; soft-cap behaviour from lib/economy/economy.mjs claimDaily/applyFloor.

findings.finding: BOT MATCHES: KEEP THEM UNSTAKED AT LAUNCH; IF STAKED LATER, CAP THEM SO FARMING CANNOT BEAT WATCHING AN AD. A house-banked bot is a faucet whenever the population beats it and a sink whenever it beats the population, and any balance-aware tuning of it is rigging. The clean answer with a 54-question bank (memorisable, so bots become farmable within days) is: bot duels pay XP, streak and quest progress but zero coins. If staked bot duels are ever added: only at s_min (10 coins), fee applies, bot accuracy is a fixed published table per difficulty derived from the human population's measured accuracy on the same questions (so the bot is by construction a median opponent, not a house edge), and a daily net-win cap from bots of 1 AE (50 coins). The inequality that makes farming pointless: at p=0.7 versus the bot, EV per 10-coin duel is 2.6 coins, about 78 coins per hour at 2 minutes a duel; one rewarded ad pays 50 coins in 30-45 seconds (4,000-6,000 coins per hour if the cap allowed it). The ad is 50-75x more coin-efficient than farming a bot, so nobody rational farms.
findings.evidence: EV and per-hour yields computed in the scratchpad script; existing bot disclosure obligation recorded in docs/money/legal-merge.json ('preserve and strengthen the existing bot disclosure'); rewarded ad max duration 30 s (60 s with high-engagement ads) per https://support.google.com/admob/answer/7311747.

findings.finding: LOSS-STREAK PROTECTION THAT IS NOT RIGGING. A 3-loss streak is common, not a signal: P(3 straight losses in a 4-duel session at p=0.5) = 18.8%, and P(at least one 3-loss streak within 10 duels) = 50.8%. Permitted levers (none touches the contest): (1) after 3 consecutive staked losses, offer a 'double-coin ad' once per day (100 coins in the US) - it is revenue-positive, honest and the player chooses it; (2) suggest, never force, one tier down, with the ruin table's reasoning in one line ('at this balance you can lose 3 in a row and still play'); (3) an unstaked friendly duel is always one tap away; (4) skill-based matchmaking on a rating computed from results only, applied to everyone identically and disclosed in the rules screen - this changes WHO you meet, not what you are asked or how the bot plays; (5) the floor top-up. FORBIDDEN, and the config engine must stay structurally unable to express them: easier questions for losers, weaker bots for low balances, timer slack, or question selection seeded by the player's known-correct history.
findings.evidence: Streak probabilities computed exactly in the scratchpad script; economy.mjs header already commits to the structural inability ('it has no notion of question difficulty, bot skill or match outcome').

findings.finding: WHY BALANCE-CONDITIONED DIFFICULTY IS BOTH AN ETHICS AND AN FTC PROBLEM. Ethics: the product's whole claim is that the duel and the Conviction badge measure knowledge; secretly softening questions or bots for a losing player makes the win a lie to the winner, the loss a lie to the opponent who faced harder questions for the same stake, and the badge a fabricated knowledge claim. Law: 15 U.S.C. 45(a)(1) declares 'unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce' unlawful; a game that represents itself as a fair, skill-decided contest for a staked pot while conditioning outcomes on balance makes a material misrepresentation on which players base the decision to watch ads and stake. The FTC has already used exactly this theory against games: Epic Games paid $245 million (order finalised 14 Mar 2023, complaint 19 Dec 2022) over dark-pattern design that tricked users, and HoYoverse paid $20 million (17 Jan 2025) because banners 'gave players the impression that they will have better odds ... than they have in reality' and a multi-tier currency 'misleads consumers about the amount of money that players spend'. The FTC's 2022 staff report lists 'Intermediate Currency: Hiding the real cost by requiring consumers to buy things with virtual currency' and 'Making the free version of a game so cumbersome and labor-intensive that the player is induced to unlock new features' as dark patterns. In the EU, the CPC Network's Key Principles (21 Mar 2025) rest on UCPD Arts 5-9 and forbid 'practices distorting the economic behavior of consumers by designing video games in ways that force the consumers to spend more'. Note the FACT//DUEL coin is NOT purchasable, which keeps it outside the CPC principles' definition (currencies 'purchased with real-world monetary value') - that boundary is a design asset and must never be crossed with a coin pack.
findings.evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/45; https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/1923203-epic-games-matter; https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/01/genshin-impact-game-developer-will-be-banned-selling-lootboxes-teens-under-16-without-parental; FTC 'Bringing Dark Patterns to Light' (Sept 2022) PDF https://www.ftc.gov/system/files/ftc_gov/pdf/P214800%20Dark%20Patterns%20Report%209.14.2022%20-%20FINAL.pdf; CPC Key Principles PDF https://commission.europa.eu/document/download/8af13e88-6540-436c-b137-9853e7fe866a_en?filename=Key%20principles%20on%20in-game%20virtual%20currencies.pdf.

findings.finding: LTV MODEL AND LEVER RANKING. ARPDAU = ads_per_DAU x eCPM / 1000, where ads_per_DAU = sessions_per_day x ads_per_session x watch_rate. LTV(H) = ARPDAU x Lifetime_days(H), Lifetime_days = 1 + sum over d of R(d). Fitting a power law through the GameAnalytics CY2025 medians (D1 22%, D30 0.74%; the fit predicts D7 3.2% against the published 'just under 4%') gives lifetime days of 2.12 at 90 days, 2.28 at 180, 2.44 at 365; the P75 curve (30% / 6.5% / 1.7%) gives 3.13 / 3.57 / 4.08; NA median (23.28 / 4.97 / 1.18) gives 2.53 / 2.83 / 3.15. Worked examples at 2 ads per DAU (= 3.85 sessions x 2 ads x 26% watch rate; the watch rate is an ASSUMPTION, UNVERIFIED): US eCPM $27.32 -> ARPDAU 5.5 cents -> LTV180 $0.124 median, $0.195 at P75 retention. Germany (eCPM $13.13) -> 2.6 cents -> $0.060 / $0.094. UK ($19.18) -> 3.8 cents -> $0.087 / $0.137. France ($10.22) -> 2.0 cents -> $0.047 / $0.073. India at an ILLUSTRATIVE $2-$4 eCPM (UNVERIFIED) -> 0.4-0.8 cents -> $0.009-$0.018 / $0.014-$0.029. Sanity anchor: MAG Interactive's QuizDuel-led portfolio reports ARPDAU of 9.0 US cents (9 months) / 8.8 cents (Q3 2025/26) from IAP plus ads, so a 5.5-cent US ads-only ARPDAU is plausible-high, not conservative. Lever ranking, by achievable headroom given every factor is multiplicative: (1) retention - median to P75 raises lifetime days 57% (2.28 to 3.57) and it compounds with every other lever; (2) ads per session - 1 to 2 doubles LTV but is bounded by tolerance and by the 20/day cap; (3) geo/platform mix - eCPM spans 10x between the US and the cheapest verified market and is exogenous per user, so it is a targeting lever (acquire US/UK first), not a design lever; (4) sessions per day - already at the 3.85 median in the model, hardest to move. A 4-ads-per-DAU US player at P75 retention is worth $0.39 over 180 days; the same player in India at $2 eCPM is worth $0.03. The repo records that CAC is unsourced (numbers.md section 5.6), so whether any of these LTVs clear acquisition cost cannot be stated.
findings.evidence: Computed in the scratchpad script from: https://www.gameanalytics.com/reports/2026-mobile-pc-gaming-benchmarks (retention percentiles, sessions/day); Tenjin/CAS.AI Q2 2024 charts (eCPM); MAG Interactive Q3 2025/26 interim report lines 23-32 and 151 (ARPDAU 8.8 / 9.0 US cents, DAU 0.9M, MAU 2.2M) https://storage.mfn.se/8d863483-ccc8-4f02-b0c5-d37d899b23e8/mag-interim-report-eng-2025-26-q3.pdf (fetched and grepped).

findings.finding: AD-FRAUD IS THE ECONOMY'S REAL ATTACK SURFACE, NOT WHALES. A spoofed completion callback mints coins for free. Google's server-side verification exists for exactly 'applications where reward validity is critical (for example, the reward affects your app's in-game economy)': the callback is ECDSA-signed with a key_id the server verifies against Google's public key set. The economy must pay only on a verified receipt (provider.verify exists as an optional method in lib/ads/provider.mjs; make it mandatory for any provider that mints coins), keep the adId idempotency window (already 64 ids), the 45 s cooldown and the 20/day cap, and treat a browser-only rewarded ad with no server callback as paying into a separate, non-stakeable 'practice-only' balance. Also: the web build has no verified rewarded-eCPM benchmark at all - every eCPM above is in-app SDK data; web rewarded eCPM is UNVERIFIED and the coin table must be re-derived from realised web eCPM within the first month.
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/admob/android/ssv (SSV definition, ECDSA signature, key_id, quoted rationale); lib/ads/provider.mjs (verify optional, serverVerified flag); lib/economy/economy.mjs earnFromAd guards.

findings.finding: RETENTION IS THE ECONOMY'S BINDING CONSTRAINT, AND HISTORY SAYS TRIVIA DIES OF IT. Deconstructor of Fun's read of Sensor Tower's 2025 ad-monetisation report: about $12 billion of mobile-game ad revenue across 19 countries, 2.4 trillion impressions, ads at 23% of net mobile-game revenue in those countries, ad revenue growing 16% a year since 2020 versus IAP about 3%, and rewarded videos commanding '30-100x higher prices per impression' than other formats - the format choice is right. But the repo's own evidence base shows Trivia Royale reached 2.5M downloads and 45% D1 and still closed within eight months, and HQ Trivia fell to 3.35% of peak downloads before shutting - monetisation and long-tail retention, not distribution, killed them. The coin economy therefore should be judged on D7/D30 movement, not on ARPDAU, in its first quarter.
findings.evidence: https://www.deconstructoroffun.com/blog/5-numbers-hiding-in-plain-sight-sensor-towers-ad-monetization-report (Josh Chandley, 3 Aug 2025); Sensor Tower report landing page https://sensortower.com/blog/gaming-deep-dive-ad-monetization-report (June 2026, figures gated); public/product/investor/numbers.md rows on Trivia Royale and HQ Trivia (TechCrunch and SEC Form D citations therein).

findings.finding: SOURCE GAPS STATED PLAINLY. (a) Supercell/King talks: the only Supercell economy-adjacent talk findable on GDC Vault without search was Eino Joas, 'Clash of Clans: Bigger, Better, Battle Pass' (GDC 2020, https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1026741/-Clash-of-Clans-Bigger); no King economy talk could be located, so none is cited. (b) Deconstructor of Fun's rewarded-video guide and hybrid-monetisation posts returned 404 at every slug tried; only the Sensor Tower numbers post is cited. (c) The rewarded-ad opt-in/watch rate (26% used above) is an assumption with no source. (d) All eCPM data is Q2 2024 in-app SDK data; 2025-2026 per-country rewarded eCPMs exist in Tenjin's report only as charts that the text does not quantify and were not re-published for later quarters on that page. (e) The web-search budget for this session was exhausted before this lane started; every source above was reached by direct fetch of a known or repo-cited URL.
findings.evidence: Tool results in this session: 404s on guessed DoF slugs; GDC Vault browse results for 'supercell', 'candy crush', 'king digital', 'free-to-play economy'; WebSearch refusals.

recommendations.what: Replace DEFAULT_CONFIG.adReward in /home/user/fact-duel/lib/economy/economy.mjs with the eCPM-derived table: US 50, GB 35, DE 25, FR 20, IN 10 (floor), '*' 10 (floor); add adRewardMin = stakes[0] and a server-side job that recomputes R_g weekly from trailing-28-day realised rewarded eCPM (EMA alpha 0.3) against a per-season frozen US reference.
recommendations.why: The current GB/DE/FR values over-pay the EU by 1.3-2x against the only verifiable per-country data, breaking the 'one ad = same revenue everywhere' rule; the floor rule guarantees one ad always buys one duel in every geo.

recommendations.what: Add a disclosed arena fee: 0% at the 10 and 25 tiers, 10% of the pot at 50-250, 15% at a new 500 tier unlocked above the 5,000 soft cap; implement as a burn leg from escrow to a sink account in lib/ledger/intents.mjs so settlement still exhausts escrow exactly; change every 'winner takes the pot' string to state the fee before commit.
recommendations.why: It is the only sink that scales with volume and stake, it is what makes the steady-state balance finite (B* = F/(n_d x r x phi) = 5,000 at the base case), and undisclosed fees are the exact 'hidden cost' pattern the FTC and CPC name.

recommendations.what: Keep bot duels unstaked (XP, streak and quest progress only). If staked bot play is ever added, restrict it to the 10-coin tier, apply the fee, publish the bot accuracy table derived from human population accuracy, and cap daily net bot winnings at 50 coins.
recommendations.why: With a 54-question bank bots become farmable within days; unstaked bots are neither a faucet nor a sink and cannot feel rigged; the ad-vs-farm inequality (about 50-75x) already removes the incentive.

recommendations.what: Pay coins only on a server-verified ad receipt: make provider.verify mandatory for any provider that mints stakeable coins (AdMob SSV, ECDSA-signed callback), and route unverified browser-only rewarded ads to a non-stakeable practice-only balance.
recommendations.why: A spoofed completion is a free mint and the single largest economy exploit; Google's own docs say SSV is for 'the reward affects your app's in-game economy'.

recommendations.what: Codify the honesty rule in the config schema and tests: the economy and matchmaking modules must have no input from question difficulty, bot skill or balance-conditioned selection; add a test that asserts the config type cannot express a difficulty or bot-skill field, and put the rule in the Rules screen ('questions and opponents are never chosen based on your balance or results').
recommendations.why: Ethics (the badge is a knowledge claim) and law (15 U.S.C. 45(a)(1); Epic $245M and HoYoverse $20M precedents on deceptive game design and odds).

recommendations.what: Ship loss-streak protection as: a once-daily double-coin ad after 3 consecutive staked losses, a tier-down suggestion with the ruin reasoning in one line, an always-available unstaked friendly duel, disclosed skill-based matchmaking, and a floor top-up to 20 coins (down from 25) every 6 h.
recommendations.why: Three-loss streaks happen in half of all 10-duel runs at p=0.5; these levers reduce lockout and rage-quit without touching the contest, and the double-coin ad is revenue-positive.

recommendations.what: Set a quest/streak grant budget of at most 30 coins per player-day and pair every quest grant with a sink (staked duels, drills, expedition entries); never add balance decay.
recommendations.why: Grants are the non-zero-sum faucet; pairing them with sinks keeps the sink/faucet ratio on target (>= 0.35 at launch, 0.6 by month 3) without a decay that reads as theft.

recommendations.what: Instrument, from day one: realised rewarded eCPM by country and platform, ads per DAU (and the opt-in rate), sink/faucet ratio, total coin supply per DAU, fee burn, share of balances above the soft cap, and D1/D7/D30 versus the GameAnalytics medians; re-derive the coin table from realised web eCPM after 30 days.
recommendations.why: India's eCPM, the web rewarded eCPM and the watch rate are all unverified; the model's biggest inputs must come from the product's own data.

recommendations.what: Acquire US and UK users first; treat India as a retention and liquidity market (opponent supply), not a revenue market, until realised eCPM is known.
recommendations.why: eCPM spans roughly 10x between the US and the cheapest verified markets and is a targeting lever, not a design lever; at an illustrative $2-4 eCPM an Indian player is worth about 5-15% of a US player over 180 days.

recommendations.what: Model the economy in Machinations (or a Monte Carlo script in tests/) with three personas - ad-watcher, skilled non-watcher, lapsed - and check that balance distributions stabilise below the soft cap within 30 simulated days before launch.
recommendations.why: The B* derivation is a mean-field estimate; persona simulation is the standard F2P method for catching runaway accumulation and lockout tails before players do.

risks: India eCPM is unverified anywhere reachable; if realised India eCPM is near the Brazil/Mexico Android level ($3), the 10-coin floor means India coins carry about half the anchor revenue value, and Indian players then net-export coins into cross-geo duels; bound this by monitoring the share of global coin supply minted in floored geos and, if it exceeds about 25%, region-locking the 100+ tiers.

Every eCPM cited is Q2 2024 in-app SDK data; FACT//DUEL is a web app with no SDK mediation, no device IDs and a 54-question bank, so realised eCPM could be several times lower and the whole coin table must be re-derived from live data within 30 days.

The rewarded-ad watch rate (26% assumed) has no source; at 10% the US ARPDAU falls to about 2 cents and the 2-ads-per-session income assumption behind the stake ladder fails, which would make the 50-coin tier feel expensive.

A 54-question bank makes staked play exploitable by memorisation (veterans versus newcomers) regardless of bot policy; the economy cannot fix a content-size problem, and staked P2P at 100+ coins should not open until the bank is in the thousands.
The arena fee changes the founder's 'winner takes the pot' promise; shipping the fee without changing every string and the Rules screen is itself the hidden-cost pattern the FTC and CPC name.

Any future coin pack for money would pull the coin inside the CPC principles and the FTC's 'intermediate currency' dark-pattern category and would reopen the gambling analysis already recorded in docs/money/legal-merge.json; the no-purchase rule is load-bearing for the legal position, not just the economy.
Ad-completion spoofing is a free mint; without mandatory server-side verification the fee and caps are irrelevant.

Retention, not ARPDAU, decides whether any of this matters: median D30 under 1% means the resident base is tiny, and the repo's own evidence shows trivia products with elite D1 still died within a year.
